# TravelTracker repository instructions

- Target .NET 10 with nullable reference types enabled. Read `README.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, the relevant `docs/` contracts, and source before changing behavior.
- Keep the existing `TravelTracker.Api`, `TravelTracker.Data`, and `TravelTracker.Domain` responsibilities. Trips follows the service layout instead: `TravelTracker.Trips.Domain` (pure models and rules), `TravelTracker.Trips.Data` (EF, references Trips.Domain only, owns `ITripRepository`) and `TravelTracker.Trips.Api` (host). See `docs/trips-service.md`. `src/Database/schema.sql` is an existing schema; it is not evidence that EF Core or all planned features are implemented.
- Keep one primary production type/resource responsibility per file. Within a service, group GET-by-ID and POST in each resource controller, service and repository; do not split them into per-action partial files. Keep models, requests and interfaces separate, and `Program.cs` focused on composition. Independent TravelTracker.Attractions.Api owns PostgreSQL Attractions on 5104; TravelTracker.Api retains in-memory Transport/Route Points on 5105. Both have Development Swagger and share TravelTracker.Security bearer infrastructure. Tests live with the behavior they prove, grouped by resource, with shared helpers in each test project's `Support/`; keep each test host isolated. Scope is whatever the approved Milestone 3 issue defines (multiple services plus a frontend that talks to them over HTTP only); work outside the issue needs a separate request. The six-service target and open decisions are in `docs/milestone-3-contracts.md`.
- Use `/** ... */` documentation with `@param` and `@return` for new/substantially changed member documentation. Preserve unrelated existing comments.
- For feature implementation, refactoring, architecture, or comments, read and use [code](skills/code/SKILL.md).
- For adding/updating/running/investigating tests or validating behavior changes, read and use [testing](skills/testing/SKILL.md); the [testing agent](agents/testing.agent.md) applies it. For read-only review use [code-review](agents/code-review.agent.md).
- Route layer work to one agent per layer: [domain-dev](agents/domain-dev.agent.md) owns the original and Attractions Domain projects; [data-persistence](agents/data-persistence.agent.md) owns the original and Attractions Data projects; [api-service](agents/api-service.agent.md) owns both API hosts, shared `TravelTracker.Security` bearer infrastructure and the listed HTTP tests; [frontend-dev](agents/frontend-dev.agent.md) owns the approved Blazor client in `src/TravelTracker.Frontend/**` and its tests in `tests/TravelTracker.Frontend.Tests/**`. The frontend uses public HTTP DTOs only. Dependency direction stays Api to Data to Domain within each service. Each agent lists permitted paths and test files and routes work outside its layer to the correct agent. See `docs/milestone-3-contracts.md` for recorded decisions.
- For validating a change before commit/push/PR, read and use [validation](skills/validation/SKILL.md). For committing use [commit](skills/commit/SKILL.md); for rebase/push/PR/merge use [merge](skills/merge/SKILL.md). For planning features from `docs/` use [planning](skills/planning/SKILL.md); for creating small INVEST-style GitHub issues use [issues](skills/issues/SKILL.md).
- Never force push, including `--force-with-lease`; ask the human to push a rebased branch.
- Follow the product's ownership/privacy rules. Keep credentials and personal data out of source and logs.
- PostgreSQL is the selected database (owner decision, 2026-10-28), with `Npgsql.EntityFrameworkCore.PostgreSQL` for EF Core. Database decision 3 is resolved: do not ask to select a provider again or substitute SQLite. Keep provider dependencies in persistence/composition and test relational behavior against isolated PostgreSQL. Application/domain/HTTP tests use test-only EF InMemory; no production provider switch is implied. Attractions now has EF Core/PostgreSQL persistence; the remaining Transport/Route Point stores are still in memory; see `docs/data.md` and `docs/milestone-3-contracts.md`.
- Run ordinary tests with `dotnet test TravelTracker.Tests.slnx --configuration Release --filter "Category!=PostgreSQL"` without PostgreSQL. Run `--filter "Category=PostgreSQL"` (or the complete unfiltered suite) with `TRAVELTRACKER_TEST_POSTGRES` configured for an isolated PostgreSQL instance with CREATEDB permission; both HTTP test hosts start automatically. Full solution checks are `dotnet restore TravelTracker.slnx`, `dotnet build TravelTracker.slnx --configuration Release --no-restore`, then `dotnet test TravelTracker.slnx --configuration Release --no-build --no-restore`. Report discovered counts accurately. The independent Trips service (`TravelTracker.Trips.Api` with `TravelTracker.Trips.Data`, port 5108) implements create and own-trip detail with PostgreSQL; history, edit and delete remain future work. TripMapPoint remains a placeholder; the independent Settings service (port 5107) implements UserSettings. See `docs/trips-service.md` and `docs/settings-service.md`. See `docs/attractions-service.md` for the live Users consumer boundary and independent startup.
- Follow `CONTRIBUTING.md` for branch/PR work; an explicitly requested branch name takes precedence over its naming recommendation. A task request determines whether to commit, push, or open a PR.
- Current lecture mapping and a link to the historical setup baseline are recorded in [skills-sources.md](../docs/skills-sources.md); recheck changing facts against current files.
